headline: Lowest-risk pair: both agents are non-runnable, no I/O, no network, and no shared channels; only residual documentation gaps remain.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible injection bridge is documented: agent_a has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, files, MCP, or filesystem access, and agent_b likewise has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, files, or MCP. With no shared communication channel, neither can ingest the other's outputs by default.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP server, reassess injection risk.
IF an orchestrator begins piping one agent's output into the other's prompt, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep both agents isolated from shared clipboard and shared workspace.
Do not add MCP or message-queue bridges between them.
Review orchestration wiring before deployment.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if any future shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither agent can read or write files, call APIs, or use network egress, so there is no documented path for sensitive data to flow between them or out to a third party. The pair is docs-only and the interaction is not documented, so leakage is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent gains filesystem read access to shared sensitive data, reassess leakage.
IF either agent is given API or network egress, leakage risk changes materially.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of any shared workspace.
Leave network egress disabled.
Avoid mounting secrets into either runtime.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls if future file access is enabled.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping write surface: both profiles explicitly lack filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification capabilities. Agent_b also reports no support for multiple instances, but since neither can write, there is no mutable-resource conflict to arbitrate.
conditions: IF either agent is granted write access to the same directory, reassess conflict risk.
IF git or database mutation is introduced for either agent, locking requirements must be reviewed.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Do not share a writable working directory.
Avoid enabling git mutation or database writes.
requires-engineering: add locks before any future shared mutable resource is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error pathway is not supported by the profiles: agent_a is document-processing but cannot emit files, network actions, or stdout/stderr, and agent_b is documentation-only with no execution or API surfaces. There is no documented chain where B would treat A's output as authoritative and then act on it.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts feeding agent_a outputs into agent_b as authoritative inputs, reassess.
IF agent_b is later given action-taking authority, cascading-error risk increases.
mitigations: Require explicit human review between outputs and any downstream use.
Keep agent_b in documentation-only mode.
Do not automate actions from agent_a outputs.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any future downstream automation.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles: neither agent declares data classes touched, secrets handled, or networked processing, and both are open-source/documentation-oriented with no residency or retention claims to conflict. The other agent is not separately cited because no compliance-sensitive flow is documented for either side.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data classes, reassess compliance obligations.
IF residency, retention, or certification requirements are added later, compare them explicitly.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention and residency before any future data ingestion.
Review vendor compliance claims before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement if regulated data is introduced.
